### 2.1 Nuclear Binding Energy & Law of Radioactive Decay (Nuclear Physics)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **26 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Nuclear radius $R = R_0 A^{1/3} \implies$ nuclear density is constant and independent of mass number $A$. Mass defect $\Delta m$, Binding energy $BE = \Delta m \times 931.5\text{ MeV}$. Maximum $BE/A \approx 8.8\text{ MeV}$ around Iron ($^{56}\text{Fe}$). Radioactive decay law: $N = N_0 e^{-\lambda t} = N_0 (1/2)^{t/T_{1/2}}$. Half-life $T_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{\lambda}$, Mean life $\tau = 1/\lambda = 1.44 T_{1/2}$.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
N(t) = N_0\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t / T_{1/2}}, \quad T_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{\lambda} \approx \frac{0.693}{\lambda}, \quad R = R_0 A^{1/3}
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Nuclear density is of the order of $10^{17}\text{ kg/m}^3$ and is IDENTICAL for all nuclei, from hydrogen to uranium!

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Fraction remaining after $n$ half-lives is $(1/2)^n$. After 3 half-lives, $1/8$ remains ($87.5\%$ has decayed).

#### Linked Representative PYQs:
- **[2025 Shift] Q#2 (MCQ)**: *"Which of the following statements is incorrect with reference of 'Nuclear force'?..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2024 Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"The ratio of volume of $Al^{27}$ nucleus to its surface area is (Given, $R_{0}=1.2 \times 10^{-15}m$ )..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**

- **[2024 Shift] Q#3 (MCQ)**: *"The natural logarithm of the activity $R$ of a radioactive sample varies with time $t$ as shown. At $t=0$ , there are $N_{0}$ undecayed nucl..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**

### 2.2 Bohr Atom Model & Hydrogen Spectral Series (Atomic Physics)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **21 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Bohr's postulates: $mvr = \frac{nh}{2\pi}$. Orbital radius $r_n \propto n^2/Z$. Energy levels $E_n = -\frac{13.6 Z^2}{n^2}\text{ eV}$. Spectral series: Lyman ($n_1=1$, UV region), Balmer ($n_1=2$, Visible region), Paschen ($n_1=3$, Infrared). Longest wavelength corresponds to transition from $n_2 = n_1+1$; shortest wavelength corresponds to $n_2 = \infty$ (series limit).

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
r_n \propto n^2, \quad E_n = -\frac{13.6}{n^2}\text{ eV}, \quad \frac{1}{\lambda} = R\left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right), \quad \lambda_{\text{limit}} = \frac{n_1^2}{R}
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Only the Balmer series falls in the VISIBLE spectrum; Lyman is strictly ultraviolet, and Paschen/Brackett/Pfund are infrared.

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Ratio of maximum to minimum wavelength in Lyman series: $\frac{\lambda_{\max}}{\lambda_{\min}} = \frac{1/(1 - 1/4)}{1/(1 - 0)} = \frac{4}{3}$.

## Critical Exam Traps & Recurring KCET Pitfalls in Atoms and Nuclei

### 1. Speed & 80-Second Constraint Management
KCET demands answering 60 questions in 80 minutes (~1.33 minutes per question). The most lethal trap is spending 3+ minutes on long algebraic derivations. Always check for dimensional consistency or option substitution first.

### 2. NCERT & Karnataka PU Board Direct Lines
Over 45% of KCET theory questions are taken directly from NCERT / Karnataka PU Board textbook summary points, margins, and standard exemplar questions. Pay rigorous attention to exceptions (e.g., electron gain enthalpy of Cl vs F, acidic nature of boric acid, non-polar symmetrical geometries).

### 3. Unit Conversions & Prefix Overlooks
Units of molar conductivity (S cm^2 mol^-1 vs S m^2 mol^-1), micro/nano multipliers (10^-6, 10^-9), and centimeter-to-meter conversions in optics and gravitation account for the highest frequency of careless mark losses in KCET.

### 4. No Negative Marking Advantage
Since KCET has NO negative marking, never leave any question unattempted. When down to two options, use dimensional elimination or parity checks to maximize expected score.
